I am a second-year Ph.D. student studying chemical engineering at MIT. I am generally interested in developing and applying GPU-based nonlinear programming techniques for dynamic optimization. My development work is focused on parametric sensitivity-based adaptive mesh relocation on GPU and GPU-based batched interior-point methods for nonlinear programs. My applied work is about parameter estimation and optimal control for systems biology and energy systems. For fun, I like to go to the gym, run along the Charles River, and play video games.

text: Research My research develops GPU-based nonlinear programming methods for dynamic optimization, where differential-algebraic equation (DAE) constraints are discretized into large, structured nonlinear programs. I implement these methods as open-source Julia software, built on ExaModels.jl and MadNLP.jl . These methods are then applied to parameter estimation and optimal control problems across a variety of fields in process systems engineering. Scalable Dynamic Optimization with GPUs Dynamic optimization problems can be solved with sequential methods, which integrate the DAEs with a time-stepping solver, or with simultaneous methods, which discretize the DAEs over the full horizon into a single large nonlinear program. The repetitive structure of simultaneous formulations maps naturally onto GPUs. I develop ExaModelsCollocation.jl to formulate these problems with orthogonal collocation, and study how GPU computing changes the trade-offs between sequential and simultaneous methods [C1] . Simultaneous methods require a sufficiently fine and properly distributed discretization mesh for accurate solution profiles. However, the mesh layout must be chosen prior to solving the problem. I am developing parametric sensitivity-based adaptive mesh relocation strategies for GPU-based nonlinear solvers, which use the sensitivities to efficiently update state trajectories upon relocating mesh nodes, building on ParametricNLPModels.jl . I am also developing GPU-based batched interior-point methods for solving weakly coupled multi-scenario nonlinear programs. Orthogonal collocation versus implicit Euler for z′ = (z − 1) 2 , z(0) = −3. Mesh relocation example from ExaModelsCollocation.jl. Estimation and Control Applications I apply these methods to parameter estimation and optimal control problems in process systems engineering, including systems biology and energy systems. For example, ExaModelsPEtab.jl formulates parameter estimation problems from systems biology as nonlinear programs that can be solved efficiently on GPUs.

text: Software I develop and contribute to open-source Julia packages for dynamic optimization and GPU-accelerated nonlinear programming, mostly around ExaModels.jl and MadNLP.jl . ExaModelsCollocation.jl : Helper functions for formulating dynamic optimization problems via orthogonal collocation in ExaModels.jl, with support for adaptive meshes and unknown time horizons. I am the main developer of the package. ExaModelsPEtab.jl : Formulates PEtab parameter estimation problems as ExaModels using orthogonal collocation, which can then be solved with MadNLP on CPUs or GPUs. I am the main developer and used it for the systems biology benchmarks in [C1] . ParametricNLPModels.jl (Developer) : A data structure for computing parametric sensitivities in nonlinear programming models, built on NLPModels.jl. I wrote the parametric Jacobian and Hessian interface. ExaModels.jl (Contributor) : A sparse automatic differentiation and algebraic modeling tool for nonlinear programs on CPUs and GPUs. I am adding automatic differentiation with respect to parameters, which computes the parametric constraint Jacobian and Lagrangian Hessian needed for sensitivity calculations. MadNLP.jl (Contributor) : A nonlinear programming solver based on the filter line-search interior-point method, with GPU support. I am adding parametric sensitivity calculations from derivatives with respect to parameters. EOptInterface.jl : An abstraction layer for optimizing componentized equation-oriented models built in ModelingToolkit.jl using JuMP.jl. I was the main developer from 2024 to 2025 as an undergraduate in the PSOR Lab [J1] .
